children: is set to hold a Capital Market Day in St. Louis, Missouri, on September 22. It is the first time the beer giant has held the event in St. Louis since 2010, when the sector-rattling merger between InBev and Anheuser-Busch was only two years old.
Ahead of the event, RBC Capital Markets analyst James Edwardes Jones highlighted that is the first time that the firm can remember, Anheuser-Busch InBev

is approaching a Capital Markets Day event needing to do no more than demonstrate that it can continue to deliver 4% to 8% organic EBITDA growth and is not going to have any "rushes of blood to the head" in terms of capital allocation.

Edwardes Jones thinks if BUD's management can underpin confidence in the organic EBITDA growth things, the strong share price performance should continue as the share price trends towards RBC's price target of €93.
have solidly outperformed other beer and spirits stocks over the last year.

Looking back, Belgium-based InBev acquired Anheuser-Busch in 2008 in an all-cash deal worth about $52B. The transaction ended roughly 150 years of independence for the St. Louis brewer behind Budweiser, Bud Light, and Michelob and created the global beer behemoth Anheuser-Busch InBev
. The combined company became the world’s largest brewer, bringing Anheuser-Busch’s U.S. portfolio together with InBev brands such as Stella Artois, Beck’s, and Brahma.

title: Back to St. Louis: Anheuser-Busch's Capital Market Day is on tap
